title_en: Sun Wukong, the Monkey Who Defied Heaven
core_summary: A monkey born from stone, with no parents and no place in the cosmic order, seizes power, strikes his own name from the ledger of death, and wars against heaven itself — until the Buddha seals him under a mountain, and centuries later he is freed into a journey that gives his defiance meaning.
central_conflict: An individual of immense power refusing the place a rigid celestial bureaucracy assigns him — freedom and self-definition versus imposed order and hierarchy.
cultural_meaning: Wukong is China's oldest anti-hero: what happens when a system humiliates someone too powerful, too free and too proud to obey. His rebellion is not nihilism but a demand to matter on his own terms; his later journey is that wild force finding purpose without being broken.
emotional_tone: defiant, electric, proud, with an undercurrent of loneliness — he has no family and no given place
global_reader_angle: Everyone has felt unseen, boxed in, told to stay in their lane. Wukong is the part of us that refuses. Lead with that universal defiance, then explain the celestial bureaucracy he is rebelling against.
must_keep_elements: true monkey nature (not human, not beast-warrior)
allowed_adaptations: which scene (birth from stone, seizing the staff, war on heaven, sealed under mountain)

visual_potential.best_scene_to_illustrate: Wukong on a mountain stone, staff in hand, facing the vast sky — small against the cosmos but unbowed.
visual_potential.composition: one-corner-half-side (Ma Yuan style), figure offset, vast negative-space sky, a single cinnabar sun as the visual eye
visual_potential.color_mood: warm rice paper, deep ink, one cinnabar accent
